4th Period.workingNow: Learning table tags and adding a table to your About Me page.
4th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A complete About Me page (copied from the Example file) with header/body structure, formatted favorites text, at least one resized image with a caption, and a table.
4th Period.smartGoal: I can build a simple table so that I can organize information on my page in rows and columns.
4th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.13 — Create prototypes using structured code, organized into separate linked pages, to fulfill a design requirement.
4th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.6 — Reading closely and explaining orally how an author uses language to support ideas.
agenda: I do: model a basic <table> with rows and cells (7 min)
We do: build one row together (5 min)
You do: self-paced — add a table to your page (20 min)
Exit Ticket: what's inside a <tr> vs. a <td>? (3 min)
4th Period.connections: You've built structure, text, and images — tables are the last new tag this week. Tomorrow we put everything together and finish the page. (Self-paced today so MAP Testing pull-outs can rejoin smoothly.)

6th Period.workingNow: Continuing yesterday's pair-coded state machine in Sprite Lab — today you're adding a third state.
6th Period.weeklyDeliverable: A Sprite Lab or Game Lab project where a scene or sprite has at least three states, each triggered by an event.
6th Period.smartGoal: I can add a third state to my state machine so that my project has three distinct, event-triggered states.
6th Period.contentStandard: CA CS Standards 6-8.AP.12 — Design and iteratively develop programs that combine control structures, including compound conditionals.
6th Period.eldStandard: ELD.PI.6-8.1 — Exchanging information and ideas with others through collaborative discussions.
agenda: Mini-lesson: what's your third state, and what triggers it? (5 min)
Pair coding: build and test your third state together (27 min)
Partner test: swap and confirm all three states trigger correctly (8 min)
Exit Ticket: describe your third state and its trigger (5 min)
6th Period.connections: On Wednesday you and your partner got your own two-state design working. Today you're pushing it further — designing and building a third state, so your project has three states total, each with its own trigger.
